title: Where do the fours fall in three different ranges?
description: Counting in fours from one to two hundred, then looking between three hundred and thirty and three hundred and forty, and in two higher ranges, shows the same last two digits each time. Keeko then links the finding to leap years from the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: hundreds and thousands are whole fours, so the last two digits decide whether four divides a number. Watch for students who look at the last digit alone.

source: Make a list of the multiples of 4 from 1 to 200. Find the multiples of 4 between 330 and 340, between 1730 and 1740, and between 2030 and 2040.
video_script.why: The child lists the count in fours, finds the numbers in three ranges that end in the same two digits, and sees that the last two digits decide.
video_script.substitution: Count in fours, find the fours in each range, and read their last two digits.
video_script.anchor: a strip of number cards counting in fours up to 200, with three range cards beside it
video_script.payoff_line: The last two digits decide whether four divides a number

final_answer.value: A number is a multiple of 4 when the number formed by its last two digits is a multiple of 4
final_answer.spoken: a number is a multiple of four when the number formed by its last two digits is a multiple of four

hold_back: Answer: A number is a multiple of 4 when the number formed by its last two digits is a multiple of 4
maths_rules: the multiples of 4 from 1 to 200: 4, 8, 12, ..., 196, 200; 200 / 4 = 50 numbers
330 = 82 x 4 + 2, so it is not a multiple of 4; 332 = 4 x 83 and 336 = 4 x 84; 340 = 4 x 85 is the end of the range
100 = 25 x 4 and 1000 = 250 x 4, so hundreds and thousands are whole fours
the last two digits in every range are 32 and 36; 32 = 4 x 8 and 36 = 4 x 9
so a number is a multiple of 4 when its last two digits make a multiple of 4
video_script.design: One idea: hundreds and thousands are whole fours, so only the last two digits decide. Assumes counting in fours. Real life: leap years, from the book's own rule that they are years that are multiples of four. The three ranges stay on the board to the end.

If the number they form is a multiple of four, so is the whole number.
<bookmark mark='every'/>In every range, the last two digits are thirty two and thirty six.
